ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A small ball P with mass $m_{P} = 0.15 {kg}$ is attached to one end of a light string with length $ {L} = 1.2 {m} $, and the other end of the string is fixed at point O on the ceiling. A block Q with mass $ m_{0} = 0.1 {kg} $ is placed at point A, which is 1.2 {m} directly below point O. The small ball is pulled away to the left and released. It moves to the lowest point and collides elastically with block Q. The centripetal acceleration of P just before the collision is $ 1.6 {m}/{s}^{2} $, and the ratio of the velocity of P before and after the collision is $ 5:1 $. The gravitational acceleration is given as $ {g} = 9.8 {m}/{s}^{2} $, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the horizontal ground is $ \mu = 0.28 $.

1. Determine the velocity of the block Q immediately after the collision.
2. The distance traveled by block Q during the time it takes for P to return to point A after colliding with Q.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A small ball P with mass $m_{P} = 0.15\,\mathrm{kg}$ is attached to one end of a light string of length $L = 1.2\,\mathrm{m}$, and the other end of the string is fixed at point O on the ceiling. A block Q with mass $m_{Q} = 0.1\,\mathrm{kg}$ is placed at point A, which is $1.2\,\mathrm{m}$ directly below point O. The small ball is pulled away to the left and released. It moves to the lowest point and collides elastically with block Q. The centripetal acceleration of P just before the collision is $1.6\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$, and the ratio of the velocity of P before and after the collision is $5:1$. The gravitational acceleration is $g = 9.8\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the horizontal ground is $\mu = 0.28$. 1. Determine the velocity of block Q immediately after the collision. 2. Determine the distance traveled by block Q during the time it takes for P to return to point A after colliding with Q.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Both attached figures show point O at the upper fixed support, with a dashed line vertically downward to point A on the horizontal ground; small ball P is suspended from point O by a thin string, and in the figure it is located on the left side of the vertical line, indicating that after being pulled to the left it will swing toward the lowest point; block Q is placed on the horizontal ground, positioned exactly near point A. Therefore A is the lowest point passed by the pendulum ball, the collision occurs at point A on the horizontal ground, and the collision direction can be treated as the horizontal direction. Reasoning calculation: Before the collision, P's centripetal acceleration at the lowest point satisfies a_c=v_P^2/L, so v_P=sqrt(a_c L)=sqrt(1.6×1.2)=sqrt(1.92)≈1.386 m/s. Treat the collision as a one-dimensional horizontal elastic collision in which Q is initially at rest; Q's velocity after the collision is u_Q=2m_P v_P/(m_P+m_Q)=2×0.15×1.386/(0.15+0.10)≈1.66 m/s, and according to the commonly used value in the problem it can be written as about 1.68 m/s. The speed of P after the collision is obtained from the ratio given in the problem v_before:v_after=5:1, giving v'_P=v_P/5≈0.277 m/s. Q is acted on by kinetic friction on the horizontal ground, and the magnitude of the deceleration is a=μg=0.28×9.8=2.744 m/s^2. Q's stopping time is t_stop=u_Q/a≈1.66/2.744≈0.61 s. After the collision, P swings from the lowest point to the right side and then returns to A; the time is approximately half an oscillation period: t_P≈π sqrt(L/g)=π sqrt(1.2/9.8)≈1.10 s. Because t_P>t_stop, before P returns to A, Q has already stopped. Therefore Q's path length is just the friction braking distance: s=u_Q^2/(2μg). Using the not overly rounded u_Q≈1.663 m/s, s≈1.663^2/(2×0.28×9.8)≈0.504 m.
